about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

corpus-map.json.note: Issue #683. compare.py read the map at 34ab993 (141 entries) and flagged 629 disagreements with the blind second map; each flag has a row in resolutions.json (192 blind-right, 12 corpus-does-not-settle, 159 reference-right, 266 not-a-disagreement). sha256 is the map corrected to those rows; compared.sha256 is the map before correction. Of the 192 blind-right rows, 186 were applied as written and 6 were not: each adds a dependsOn edge that closes a dependsOn cycle (check-map no-cycles), so the entry is left as it was. Of the 12 unsettled rows, 6 were already recorded in the map as ambiguous with fate unresolved, and 6 made two further entries ambiguous (transactional-or-relationship-message-defined, transactional-or-relationship-content). The unresolvedReason of two entries that took a dependsOn edge to a definition in a corpus that was not admitted became MissingRulesData, as the correspondence table requires. The comparison's reference gained the commit it read, which check-map-review.py requires it to name. The blind mapper worked from staged inputs recorded in blind-mapping/staged-inputs.json.
